public_rationale: Marcus warns that the after-hours decline is only the beginning of further trouble. The surrounding text leaves open whether he means a further stock selloff, disruption to AI financing, or broader fallout. Selecting an intraday low as success supplies both the outcome and the measurement rule. Selecting a closing price would make a different unsupported choice. The available trading report cannot cure that ambiguity. This is not a finding that the warning was false; the submitted forecast lacks a sufficiently definite test.
limitations: This assessment concerns the forecast portion of the sentence, not the accuracy of its historical after-hours statement.
The accessible market evidence is secondary reporting.
Missing a deadline alone would warrant an open horizon, but the ambiguity here also concerns what was predicted.

statement.document_title: Jensen is reportedly about to get fired

from_speaker: The stock is already down in after hours
our_interpretation: The sentence presents the after-hours decline as the beginning of further trouble. It does not clearly specify whether that trouble means further stock losses or the broader consequences discussed around it.
Treating any subsequent intraday low as fulfillment would add a test Marcus did not supply. Requiring a particular closing price or duration would also add a test.
The problem is not merely the missing deadline. The predicted outcome itself cannot be specified reliably without choosing among materially different readings.
The historical statement about after-hours trading is background to the submitted forecast, not a separately graded claim.
criteria.support_condition: No sufficiently definite condition can be set from these words alone. Support would require identifying what further development constitutes 'just the start' without imposing an evaluator-selected stock-price or broader-crisis test.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No sufficiently definite contradiction condition follows from the wording. A recovery or a limited decline over an evaluator-selected interval would not disprove an unspecified forecast of further trouble.
